components.description: PER-4.17: up to 12 weeks of family and medical leave in a rolling year, adopted to comply with the federal FMLA, for the birth and care of a newborn, adoption or foster placement, a family member's or the employee's own serious health condition; unpaid except where accrued balances are used; job restoration on return.
components.faculty_group_note: applies to all faculty and staff employees who meet the eligibility requirements defined in this policy
components.eligible_parent_wording: The birth of a child and the care of the newborn; placement of a child with an employee in connection with the adoption or state-approved foster care; available equally to both sexes; serious health condition of a child, parent, or spouse; a serious health condition of the employee
components.service_requirement: employed by the university for at least 12 months, and at least 1250 hours during the last 12 months immediately preceding the leave
components.dual_employee_rule: each employee is entitled to 12 weeks of leave during any 12-month period for the birth or placement of a child
components.entitlement_note: 'is entitled to'; the statutory FMLA entitlement stays guaranteed though forms must be submitted.
components.duration_note: 'a maximum of 12 weeks ... in a year'; Year: twelve months measured backward from the first date family and medical leave begins. The statute states 'a total of 12 workweeks' (29 U.S.C. 2612(a)(1)).
components.medical_certification_note: For a serious health condition, a health care provider must certify that the employee is needed to care for the family member, or that the employee is unable to perform the essential functions of the position.
components.time_window: Leave for birth or placement of a child must take place within 12 months after the event; leave may begin prior to the birth or adoption
components.return_obligation: an employee who elects not to return after approved unpaid leave reimburses the university's insurance premium contribution for any complete months of unpaid leave (not if for reasons beyond the employee's control, or on retirement)
components.notice: submit the Employee Request for Family Medical Leave form (Section I to the supervisor; Section II by the health care provider to Human Resources)
components.relief_note: A leave; no relief stated, so every duty is relieved (R9).

sequence.note: Leave for the birth must be reported as family and medical leave, so FMLA runs alongside the six-week paid parental leave from its start (S1); 6 weeks of the 12 remain unpaid except for the employee's own balances (c3).

notes: Reference date 2018-03-13. Sources: 2018_00_link (PER-4.17 Family and Medical Leave); 2018_01 (Redbook Chapter 4); 2018_02 (PER-4.18 Parental Leave).

Governing documents for faculty leave are saved: PER-4.18 (paid parental leave) and PER-4.17 (FMLA) both apply to faculty; the Redbook (the University's governing document) Chapter 4 sets faculty leaves of absence and the probationary period. So missing is false (The no-policy coding (`missing`) does not apply).

Dates: PER-4.17 and PER-4.18 were captured in 2019 but list their last revision as May 17, 2017 (effective November 30, 2017), so the text is the version in force on 2018-03-13. The Redbook capture is 2018-07-15 (Chapter 4 effective 01-01-02, Art. 4.4 revised 2011).

Not components: Redbook 4.3.5 sabbatical leave (for activities that improve the faculty member's contribution to the University; not a leave a parent could take for a birth); Redbook 4.5.5 suspension with salary; PER-4.17 'disability insurance plans' (named only as benefits not continued during unpaid FMLA leave; no plan terms in the saved sources); PER-4.17 F intermittent or reduced leave schedule (part of FMLA leave for a serious health condition, within c2). PER-4.17 extends family and medical leave to a 'qualifying adult' and in-laws beyond the statute (UofL Eligibility Note); this changes who counts as family, not the member's leave.
PER-4.18 does not apply to temporary employees, student positions, trainees or house staff; tenure-stream faculty are not among these groups.

Restriction on c1 (PER-4.18): part-year employees get no parental leave pay for any part of the leave outside the appointment period; academic-year faculty may be such employees, so a birth near or in the summer can reduce the paid weeks. The documents do not say whether nine-month faculty are 'employees who work for the university during part of the year'.

Birth parent chain: PER-4.18 paid parental leave 6 weeks (c1) with FMLA 12 weeks (c2) running concurrently from its start; own accrued sick, vacation and personal balances (c3) within FMLA; tenure-clock provisions (c4, c5) and general leaves (c6, c7) unlinked and counted in no figure.
Non-birth parent chain: the same as the birth parent: PER-4.18 paid parental leave 6 weeks (c1) with FMLA 12 weeks (c2) concurrent from its start; own balances (c3) within FMLA.

Documents cited but not saved: PER 4.21 Leave of Absence without Pay (PER-4.17, Related Information); HR policy definitions page http://louisville.edu/hr/policies/definitions (PER-4.18 Definitions); the university's sick, vacation and personal leave provisions (the balances PER-4.17 A requires to be used; not named by title); PER-5.03 Grievances (PER-4.17 I.2; not about leave); Addenda to The Redbook (other faculty appointment types, Redbook 4.1.4); other Redbook chapters (Secs. 2.5.1, 2.5.5, 2.5.8, 3.1.1, 3.3.1; not about leave); the Request for Leave Form and the Employee Request for Family Medical Leave form (forms). The policy library's navigation also lists 'Other Leaves with Pay', 'Lactation Accommodations' and 'Student Pregnancy Accommodations' pages, which no policy text cites and which are not saved.
No term length or kind of term is stated; calendar omitted.
